Control Objective: Ensure identities receive only approved permissions required for their duties.
Example AWS Capability or Process: IAM policies and roles; IAM Access Analyzer; access reviews
Reference Mapping (Indicative): AWS Security Pillar; NIST CSF PR.AA; ISO A.5.15/A.5.18
Evidence Required: Identity/role inventory, policies, access approvals, analyzer findings, review records
Test Approach: Review sampled privileged and workload identities for broad grants, unused access and business justification.

Control Objective: Protect privileged human access with strong authentication and controlled role assumption.
Example AWS Capability or Process: Identity federation, MFA, IAM role trust policies, short-lived credentials
Reference Mapping (Indicative): AWS Security Pillar; NIST CSF PR.AA; ISO A.5.17
Evidence Required: MFA coverage, identity-provider settings, role trust policies, break-glass procedure
Test Approach: Verify privileged human access path, MFA enforcement, role trust restrictions and emergency-access review.

Control Objective: Limit public ingress and egress to approved business requirements.
Example AWS Capability or Process: VPC, subnet routes, security groups, network ACLs, load balancer configuration
Reference Mapping (Indicative): AWS Security Pillar; NIST CSF PR.IR; ISO A.8.20
Evidence Required: VPC/subnet/route/security-group exports, public endpoint inventory, approved data flows
Test Approach: Identify publicly reachable resources and compare effective paths with approved architecture.

Control Objective: Separate application, data and administration trust zones.
Example AWS Capability or Process: VPC design, security groups, routing, private connectivity
Reference Mapping (Indicative): AWS Security Pillar; NIST CSF PR.IR; ISO A.8.22
Evidence Required: Architecture diagram, route tables, security-group references, connectivity test results
Test Approach: Test allowed and denied paths between tiers in an authorized lab; record exceptions.

Control Objective: Capture required management activity within the approved account and region scope.
Reference Mapping (Indicative): AWS Security Pillar; NIST CSF DE.CM; ISO A.8.15/A.8.16
Evidence Required: Trail status, account/region coverage, event selectors, destination configuration
Test Approach: Verify required scope and configuration; confirm a controlled test event appears in the expected destination.

Control Objective: Protect audit records from unauthorized change or deletion and retain them appropriately.
Example AWS Capability or Process: S3 log destination controls, access policies, retention settings, CloudTrail log validation where enabled
Reference Mapping (Indicative): AWS Security Pillar; NIST CSF PR.DS/DE.CM; ISO A.8.15
Evidence Required: Bucket policy, encryption and retention settings, administrative access list, validation settings
Test Approach: Review who can read, change or delete logs; compare retention to approved policy.

Control Objective: Detect and route selected security events to accountable responders.
Example AWS Capability or Process: Amazon CloudWatch alarms and approved security monitoring workflow
Reference Mapping (Indicative): AWS Security Pillar; NIST CSF DE.CM/RS.MA; ISO A.8.16
Evidence Required: Alarm definitions, notification routing, test records, incident tickets
Test Approach: Trigger or simulate approved test events and verify alert delivery, ownership and response recording.

Control Objective: Maintain visibility of supported resource configuration and identify deviations from policy.
Example AWS Capability or Process: AWS Config recorder, resource coverage, rules or conformance packs
Reference Mapping (Indicative): AWS Security Pillar; NIST CSF PR.PS; ISO A.8.9
Evidence Required: Recorder status, resource coverage, rule definitions, compliance history, exception log
Test Approach: Confirm recording scope and evaluate selected rule results against resource configuration.

Control Objective: Ensure cloud infrastructure changes are reviewed, authorized and traceable.
Example AWS Capability or Process: Infrastructure-as-code review, CI/CD permissions, change tickets, deployment roles
Reference Mapping (Indicative): AWS Security Pillar; NIST CSF PR.PS; ISO A.8.32
Evidence Required: Pull requests, approval records, deployment logs, role permissions and exception approvals
Test Approach: Sample changes and trace each from request through approval, deployment and post-change validation.

Control Objective: Prevent disclosure of credentials and minimize long-lived access keys.
Example AWS Capability or Process: IAM roles, managed secrets, repository and pipeline secret scanning
Reference Mapping (Indicative): AWS Security Pillar; NIST CSF PR.AA; ISO A.5.17/A.8.24 where applicable
Evidence Required: Credential inventory metadata, scan results, rotation records, secret-store access policies
Test Approach: Check for unnecessary long-lived keys and validate secret handling without exposing secret values.

Control Objective: Ensure backups are protected and recovery capability is periodically demonstrated.
Example AWS Capability or Process: AWS Backup or service-native backup and restore procedures
Reference Mapping (Indicative): AWS Security Pillar; NIST CSF RC.RP; ISO A.8.13
Evidence Required: Backup policy, coverage report, access controls, restoration test and RTO/RPO approval
Test Approach: Sample critical assets and inspect backup completion and documented restoration test results.

Control Objective: Track findings, exceptions and risk acceptance through accountable closure.
Example AWS Capability or Process: Security finding workflow, ticketing, risk register, management reporting
Reference Mapping (Indicative): NIST CSF GV.OV/GV.RR; ISO risk treatment processes
Evidence Required: Finding inventory, owner and due-date fields, exception approvals, closure evidence
Test Approach: Sample findings and verify ownership, target dates, escalation, validation and residual-risk approval.
